answer: In this PoA design, identity verification is bound to a Wesolowski VDF: each proof requires a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with every result needed to compute the next. A sybil operator may create many digital clones, but cannot collapse those dependency chains into parallel GPU work to reduce wall-clock time per identity; additional hardware only multiplies cost. Thus each island, mirror, or harbor identity faces the same measurable delay, making mass fabrication physically expensive.
